1. The present appeal has been preferred by the claimant/appellant for enhancement of compensation awarded by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Patiala (for short, 'the Tribunal') vide award dated 10.01.2006 under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, whereby,
the claimant/appellant was awarded a compensation of Rs.10,000/-
Rs.10,000/ along with interest @ 6% per annum.
FACTS NOT IN DISPUTE 2.

Brief facts of the case are that on 08.04.2003, the appellant was travelling from Zirakpur to Rajpura alongwith his father Gurbax Singh on his scooter bearing registration No.PB-11-S-2895 No.PB 2895 and the same being driven by the appellant at normal speed with care and caution and when they reached within the municipal limits of Banur, a truck bearing registration No.PB No.PB-11-N-4445 (hereinafter referred to as the offending truck), came from behind, which was being driven by respondent No.1, at at a high speed, rashly and negligently, and hit the scooter of the appellant, as a result of the same, the appellant's right ankle was fractured and suffered extensive wound on the right leg and the scooter was totally damaged.
Father of the appellant received received minor injuries.
The appellant was taken to Military Hospital, Chandimandir, by his father by hiring a Maruti Van, which was coming from behind.
Since that day, the appellant is under continuous treatment, his skin grafting surgery has been conducted but the same is liable to be FAO-2114-2006 2006 (O&M) -3- conducted again.
The appellant has also suffered injuries on other parts of the body when the skin was taken from other parts for skin grafting surgery.
The appellant has been deprived of continuation of service, chances of ppromotion romotion and he has also become unfit for civil services.
The appellant has suffered huge expenses on his injuries caused by the accident.
He also suffered permanent physical disability due to the accidental injuries.
The appellant and his family has also suffered mental pain, agony due to injuries sustained by the appellant in the accident.
3. Upon notice of the claim petition, respondents appeared and denied the factum of accident/compensation.
4. From the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal fram framed ed the following issues:-

9. A perusal of the award indicates that the amount of compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is on the lower side and claimant has suffered 23% disability due to accident in question.

A perusal of award further reveals that as per income certificate the claimant was drawing salary of Rs.7,055/ Rs.7,055/- per month, in view of the salary certificate the income of claimant is assessed as Rs.7,055/-
Rs.7,055/ per month.
Moreover, award reveals that no amount was granted for future FAO-2114-2006 2006 (O&M) -5- prospects and Tribunal has not applied multiplier while calculating the compensation.

Further, a perusal of the award reveals that claimant was admitted in Military Hospital and it is admitted fact that if patient is treated in Mili Military tary Hospital, he is not entitled for reimbursement of treatment as well as medicine as these facilities are provided free of cost to the patient.
Therefore, the award requires interference by this Court.
SETTLED LAW ON COMPENSATION 10.
Hon'ble Supreme Court Court has settled the law regarding grant of compensation with respect to the disability.

The Apex Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another (2011) 1 Supreme Court Cases 343 343,, has held as under:-
General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 5.

sentences.text: The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be FAO-2114-2006 2006 (O&M) -6- compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or ccould ould have earned.

(i) All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.

(iii) The doctor who treated an injured injured-claimant claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence Jagjeet Singh vs Parma Nand And Ors on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116629291/
5 in entirety.
11. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi Se &
Ors. [(2017) 16 SCC 680] has clarified the law under Sections 166, 163-A 163 A and 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, on the following aspects:-
FAO-2114-2006 2006 (O&M) -10- (A) Deduction of personal and living expenses to determine multiplicand;
(B) Selection of multiplier depending on age of deceased; (C) Age of deceased on basis for applying multiplier; (D) Reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely,
loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, with escalation; (E) Future prospects for all categories of ppersons ersons and for different ages: with permanent job; self-employed self employed or fixed salary.
In para 46 of the said judgment, the Constitution Bench effectively affirmed the multiplier method to be used as mentioned in the table in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, 2009 ACJ 1298 (SC) .
In the age group of 15-25 15 25 years, the multiplier has to be '18' along with factoring in the extent of disability.
(b) Loss of earning capacity of the appellant with permanent disability of 31.1%
In respect of the aforesaid, the appellant has claimed compensation on what is stated to be the settled principle set out in Jagdish v. Mohan & Others, 2018 ACJ 1011 (SC) and Sandeep Khanuja v. Atul Dande &
Another, 2017 ACJ 979 (SC).
So far as the interest part is concerned, as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dara Singh @
Dhara Banjara Vs. Shyam Singh Varma 2019 ACJ 3176 and R.Valli and Others VS. Tamil Nandu State Transport Corporation (2022) 5 FAO-2114-2006 2006 (O&M) -16- Supreme Court Cases 107,
the amount so calculated shall carry an interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of realization.
